sections.skill: Classify an AI use as recommending, recognizing, forecasting or generating

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: A video site shows "Up next" suggestions based on what you watched. Which job is this?
questions.intro: Most everyday AI does one of four kinds of jobs. RECOMMENDING suggests items you might want, such as videos, products or friends. RECOGNIZING (also called classifying) puts input into categories: a face in a photo, a spoken word, a fraudulent payment. FORECASTING predicts a number or event, such as tomorrow's temperature, travel time or next month's sales. GENERATING creates new content: text, images, audio or code. One app can do several jobs, for example recognizing your voice and then generating a reply. Naming the job helps you decide what could go wrong and how to check the result.
questions.feedback: Suggesting items you might want is recommending.

sections.skill: Match each job to a familiar helper

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: The cashier knows a scanned item is a banana. Which job is that?
questions.intro: Think of four helpers in a shop. The SALES CLERK says, "People who bought this also liked that": recommending. The CASHIER scans an item and knows it is a banana, not a lemon: recognizing. The MANAGER looks at past weeks and says, "We will sell about 300 loaves on Saturday": forecasting. The SIGN PAINTER creates a brand-new poster for a sale: generating. AI systems do these same four kinds of jobs, just with software instead of people.
questions.feedback: Identifying an item is recognizing.

sections.title: Apply it

sections.skill: Use the job type to decide what to check

questions.domain: Foundation 1: What AI is and where it appears
questions.prompt: A voice app answers "Book a table for four" by booking a table for two. Speech was turned into text, then a booking was made. What should be checked first?

choices.text: Whether the booking page used AI at all
Whether the restaurant forecast was wrong
Whether the recommendations were too narrow
Whether the speech was recognized correctly

questions.correct_answer: Whether the speech was recognized correctly
questions.intro: Each job fails in its own way, so naming the job tells you what to check. A RECOMMENDER can keep showing more of the same and miss what you actually need. A RECOGNIZER can put things in the wrong category, especially with unusual examples. A FORECAST can miss sudden changes that never appeared in past data. A GENERATOR can produce fluent content that is false or copied. When one app chains jobs together, an early mistake can spread: if your speech is misrecognized, the generated reply answers the wrong question.
questions.feedback: In a chain, an early recognition error spreads to later steps.
